value.body: State governments recruit staff nurses (nursing officers in some states) for district hospitals, community health centres and medical college hospitals. The work covers ward and ICU care, medication, maternity and emergency nursing and, in rural postings, public-health programmes. Each state uses its own recruitment body.

items.label: Basic requirement
items.note: Registered nurse and midwife with the State Nursing Council

items.label: Who recruits
items.value: State health recruitment boards, PSCs or the health department
items.note: Varies by state; contract posts under the National Health Mission are also common

value.title: How you get in
value.body: Complete B.Sc Nursing (4 years) or GNM and register with the State Nursing Council. Apply to the state's staff-nurse recruitment — usually a written exam (sometimes with weight for experience), followed by document verification. Many states require the local language and domicile for some quotas.

value.title: At a glance
items: Regular posts are filled in irregular batches; contract posts are more frequent.
Shift work, including nights, is standard.
Central routes such as AIIMS NORCET and railway or ESIC notices run alongside state recruitment.
